Russia enters this fixture in exceptional form, riding a strong wave of momentum in their recent friendlies. Sbornaya has registered dominant back-to-back home victories, crushing Namibia 6-0 and defeating Iran 2-0. Aside from a minor 1-0 slip against Egypt earlier in the year, Valery Karpin's team has been highly clinical, picking up comfortable 3-0 wins over both Trinidad and Tobago and Burkina Faso to cement their formidable status.
Russia: Agkatsev; Adamov, Melyokhin, Osipenko, Beveev; Karpukas, Prutsev, Umyarov; Miranchuk, Sadulayev, Tyukavin

Nigeria carries highly inconsistent form, struggling to find stability under head coach Eric Chelle. The Super Eagles recently suffered a heavy 3-0 defeat against Guinea-Bissau in their latest Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, following a narrow 2-1 victory over Madagascar. Their friendly campaign has yielded mixed results, featuring a 2-1 loss to Portugal, a 2-2 draw with Poland.
For Russia, Konstantin Tyukavin is a strong candidate to start up front after managing 78 minutes in the victory over Iran, having previously come off the bench in the big win against Namibia.
Wilfred Ndidi is officially ruled out after picking up a knock against Guinea-Bissau, while defender Victory Akpe and goalkeeper Maduka Okoye are also sidelined.
